es.summary: El audit log de Kubernetes registró una solicitud de eliminación (verb delete) sobre un recurso deployments. Puede ser mantenimiento normal o un intento de interrumpir cargas de trabajo en producción.
es.what_it_detects: Eventos de auditoría del API server con verb igual a delete y objectRef.resource igual a deployments, es decir, la eliminación de un Deployment, por ejemplo con kubectl delete deployment o a través de la API.
es.why_it_matters: Al eliminar un Deployment se borran sus ReplicaSets y pods, y el servicio queda caído. La regla lo clasifica como Impact (ATT&CK T1498) y toma como referencia la técnica Data destruction de la Threat Matrix for Kubernetes de Microsoft.
triage_steps: Identifique objectRef.namespace, objectRef.name, user.username, user.groups, sourceIPs y userAgent. Confirme si el namespace es de producción o crítico.
Revise responseStatus.code: con 200 o 202 la eliminación se ejecutó; con 403 fue denegada, pero indica un intento.
Considere solo una vez las etapas duplicadas del mismo auditID, como RequestReceived y ResponseComplete.
Verifique si la identidad es humana, una service account o un pipeline de CI/CD o GitOps, y si existe un ticket o cambio aprobado.
Busque eventos del mismo usuario o IP en +/- 15 minutos: otros delete, deletecollection, cambios de RBAC, secrets leídos, exec en pods.
Busque autenticaciones anómalas: IP de origen nueva, userAgent inusual o uso de tokens de service account fuera del clúster.
Consulte alertas anteriores de la misma identidad, del mismo namespace y del mismo clúster.
false_positives: Retiro planificado de aplicaciones o limpieza de entornos de prueba.
Herramientas GitOps o CI/CD, como Argo CD, Flux o Helm, que eliminan recursos durante un sync o un uninstall.
Operadores o controladores que recrean Deployments como parte de su ciclo normal.
response_steps: Confirme con el dueño del namespace o del pipeline si la eliminación estaba autorizada.
Si no lo estaba, revoque o rote las credenciales o tokens usados y restrinja temporalmente los permisos RBAC de esa identidad.
Restaure el Deployment desde el repositorio GitOps, un manifiesto versionado o un respaldo, por ejemplo con Velero, y valide que el servicio funcione.
Revise el resto de la actividad de la identidad para encontrar persistencia o más impacto y documente el incidente.
es.severity_rationale: El nivel low es adecuado porque eliminar Deployments es una operación administrativa frecuente. Conviene escalar si el namespace es crítico, la identidad es inesperada o hay actividad sospechosa relacionada.

en.summary: The Kubernetes audit log recorded a delete request against a deployments resource. This can be normal maintenance or an attempt to disrupt production workloads.
en.what_it_detects: API server audit events where verb is delete and objectRef.resource is deployments, meaning a Deployment was removed, for example with kubectl delete deployment or through a direct API call.
en.why_it_matters: Deleting a Deployment also removes its ReplicaSets and pods, which takes the service down. The rule tags this as Impact (ATT&CK T1498) and cites Data destruction from the Microsoft Threat Matrix for Kubernetes.
triage_steps: Note objectRef.namespace, objectRef.name, user.username, user.groups, sourceIPs and userAgent. Check whether the namespace is production or critical.
Check responseStatus.code: 200 or 202 means the deletion went through, while 403 means it was denied but still shows an attempt.
Count duplicate stages that share one auditID, such as RequestReceived and ResponseComplete, only once.
Find out whether the identity is a human, a service account or a CI/CD or GitOps pipeline, and look for a matching ticket or approved change.
Pivot on the same user or source IP within +/- 15 minutes: other deletes, deletecollection, RBAC changes, secret reads, pod exec.
Look for unusual authentication: a new source IP, an odd userAgent, or a service account token used from outside the cluster.
Review earlier alerts for the same identity, namespace and cluster.
false_positives: Planned decommissioning of applications or cleanup of test environments.
GitOps or CI/CD tools, such as Argo CD, Flux or Helm, that prune resources during a sync or an uninstall.
Operators or controllers that recreate Deployments as part of their normal reconciliation.
response_steps: Confirm with the namespace or pipeline owner whether the deletion was authorized.
If it was not, revoke or rotate the credentials or tokens used and temporarily restrict that identity's RBAC permissions.
Restore the Deployment from the GitOps repo, a versioned manifest or a backup, for example Velero, and check that the service works.
Review the identity's other activity for persistence or further impact, and document the incident.
en.severity_rationale: Low fits because deleting Deployments is a common administrative action. Escalate when the namespace is critical, the identity is unexpected or related suspicious activity shows up.

positive.description: A user deletes the payments-api Deployment in production with kubectl and the request completes.
A service account token used from outside the cluster tries to delete a Deployment and gets denied by RBAC.

negative.description: A pod (not a deployment) is deleted, so objectRef.resource does not match.
A Deployment is scaled with a patch, so the verb is not delete.
